links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy after AI withdrawal under scaffold-first versus AI-first or unsupported training
links.effect: After withdrawal, scaffold-first groups outperformed unsupported students (24.5–24.7% vs 9.0%; ORs 3.77–3.87) and AI-first students (24.6% vs 14.4%; OR 2.19).
links.quote: Students who began with AI scaffolding achieved higher diagnostic accuracy than those given access to the AI assistant from the outset both during the subsequent intervention phase (75.2% vs 66.0%; OR 1.73, 95% CIs [1.12–2.68]) and after withdrawal (24.6% vs 14.4%; OR 2.19, 95% CIs [1.15–4.14]).

screen.practice: Sequencing reasoning scaffolding before AI assistance in training
screen.reason: The study is a randomized controlled trial in medical students evaluating pedagogical/deployment strategies (scaffolding reflective reasoning before direct answer assistance) to optimize clinical reasoning and prevent overreliance when using generative LLMs.
